objective.statement: Write notes neatly and accurately in the treble and bass clefs.
successCriteria: I put a line note's head on the line, with the line through its middle.
I fill the space with a space note's head, touching the lines above and below.
I check my note by counting from the bottom of the stave.

explanation.text: Writing a note well means the reader can see at once which line or space you mean. Draw the head as an oval, not a circle, and keep it the right size.

music.textAlternative: A treble stave with two notes on lines, G and B. The line passes through the middle of each notehead.

explanation.caption: A line note: the line runs through the middle of the notehead.

music.textAlternative: A treble stave with two notes in spaces, A and C. Each notehead fills its space, touching the lines above and below.

explanation.caption: A space note: the head fills the space, touching the line above and the line below.

explanation.text: Check your work by counting up from the bottom of the stave to your note, saying the letter names as you go. Do the check in the right clef: treble and bass use different names.

A stem is added to notes shorter than a semibreve. Stems usually go up on the right for notes below the middle line, and down on the left for notes on or above it. Stem direction is shown for neatness here; the questions in this course ask only for the pitch.

music.textAlternative: Three bass-clef notes, B on the 2nd line, C in the 2nd space and D on the 3rd line, showing how line and space notes sit on the stave.

steps: Tap B on the 2nd line and see the line pass through the middle of the notehead.
Tap C in the space above: the head fills the space exactly.
Tap D on the 3rd line. Notice line and space notes take turns going up.
demonstration.textAlternative: Three bass-clef notes, B on a line, C in a space and D on the next line, showing neat placement.

guided.prompt: Write F in the treble clef. You may use up to 1 ledger line. Any F that fits is correct.
hints: Start from the clef's reference line.
Middle C needs one ledger line.
In the treble clef the bottom line is E. Count up one letter for each line and space until you reach F.

feedback.correct: Placed neatly: counting from the bottom gave you the right spot.

mistakes.wrong-octave: That's the right letter name, but in a different octave. Check which one the question asks for.
mistakes.line-space-swap: Nearly — move it between a line and a space and check again.
mistakes.clef-confusion: That position would be right in a different clef. Look at the clef first.
mistakes.ledger-miscount: Count the ledger lines needed — one for each line above or below the stave.
mistakes.counted-from-top: Lines and spaces are counted from the bottom of the stave upwards.
mistakes.accidental-missing: The position is right, but the note needs its sharp, flat or natural.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Find a reference note and count lines and spaces from it.

recap: A line note has the line through the middle of its head; a space note fills the space.
Check by counting from the bottom of the stave, in the correct clef.
Treble and bass clefs use different names for the same lines and spaces.

mastery.completion: The lesson is complete when every step has been answered correctly (retries allowed). Only first-attempt, hint-free independent answers count as mastery evidence; guided steps never do.
